desc:
This was once considered bad, being similar to the standard joseki at <position: 26982> except that <A:M16> is too close to White's wall. That opinion had begun to change, even before AlphaGo Teach demonstrated it, because of renewed emphasis on the corner territory and the fact that the white stone at <B:P14> is also too close to White's own formation.

This is also the likely reason why AlphaGo famously attached at <C:R17> in Game 1 in the widely-viewed Challenge Match against Lee Sedol—had it jumped out to B, it expected Black to attach underneath and so prevented it in advance.

Black protects with <D:N16> or <E:N15>.
